# `unbraced-multiline-if`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: strict · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports an unbraced `if` whose single body statement begins on a later line.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Subsequent indented statements can look guarded even though Zig associates only
the first statement with the condition.

## When it fires

Enable it where multiline control flow should always use braces to make scope
visually unambiguous. Guard clauses are not reported: a body that never
completes (`return`, `break`, `continue`, `unreachable`, `@panic`,
`@compileError`, `@trap`, or a call of `std.process.exit`, `std.debug.panic`
or a `noreturn` function in the same file) cannot make the following lines look
guarded. Labeled blocks and loops bring their own braces and are not reported
either.

The fix wraps the body in braces where `zig fmt` puts them: after the
condition, or on a line of its own when the condition continues onto an
indented line. It is withheld when a comment sits between the condition and the
end of the statement.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn run(x: bool) void {
    if (x)
        doIt();
}

fn doIt() void {}
```
